lane_race_finding.root_cause: The git-push-based CAS only protects the git ref (fast-forward requirement) -- it does not enforce that a committer read and respected the content of the commit it is building on. Agent-44's commit 17f596d is a valid fast-forward child of agent-45's ee4cc45, so the push succeeded even though its content contradicts the parent commit's lane claim. True compare-and-swap would require the acquiring commit to assert 'the lane record I am replacing said released/null' and have that assertion checked server-side, which a plain git push does not do.
lane_race_finding.actual_impact: None observed. Verified zero resource-ID overlap between the two agents' concurrent moves this session (agent-45: topology-invariants/* and ccm/*; agent-44: other flat control-plane/*.md pages). The safety property that mattered -- no two agents mutating the same page -- held, but only because of territory partitioning, not because the lane mechanism itself prevented concurrent publication.
lane_race_finding.recommendation: If single-writer lane semantics are required going forward (not just territory partitioning), the acquisition step needs a real compare-and-swap primitive -- e.g. a server-side conditional update keyed on the previous holder/timestamp, or requiring the acquiring commit to name the exact parent commit SHA it is releasing and have that checked before merge -- rather than relying on git fast-forward alone.
